name: Tyler Hoffman
action: Tyler tells his dad, "Yeah, I’ll be there—I’ll grab a twelve-pack on the way." He stops by the store, picks up a twelve-pack, and arrives at the house before kickoff, staying in through the first half instead of drifting outside early.
reason: Tyler’s initial response mixed a temptation to text an excuse with a pull to just show up. Reflecting on his dad’s habit of quietly covering community college costs and his mom handing him the chip bowl last year made the obligation feel less like a chore and more like a way to match how his parents show up for him. His fatigue and pending errands still pulled against going, but that conflict made backing out feel like the easy version of himself he didn’t want to keep being. The reflective reappraisal STRENGTHENED his leaning to attend, so he committed out loud, bought the twelve-pack, arrived before kickoff, and stayed through halftime—a choice that avoids the guilt of bailing even though his own plans remain unfinished.
